chapterId.description: MUST equal ctx.itemId — this chapter's own id, e.g. 'ch_02'.

characters.description: One entry per anchored/recurring CHARACTER who appears anywhere in this chapter. A character who never appears in this chapter is omitted entirely. Empty array only if this chapter has no anchored characters at all.

id.description: The story_bible character id, verbatim (e.g. 'ira_kulkarni'). Never a display name, never invented.

states.description: This character's appearance TIMELINE through this chapter, in screen order. ONE entry per point where the appearance MATERIALLY changes — not one per shot, and not one per scene. A character who looks the same all chapter has exactly ONE entry. Each state holds from its own `from` scene until the next state's `from`; the renderer forward-fills every shot in between, so an unchanged appearance is never restated.

signature.description: Short, stable lowercase key for this exact appearance state, e.g. 'ira__white_top_jeans'. This is the STATE KEY: an identical appearance MUST reuse an identical signature, including across chapters — if the previous chapter's ledger already named this look, copy that signature verbatim. A new signature mints a whole new identity plate downstream, so only a material change earns one.

appearance.description: FULL standalone description of the character's look while this state holds: garments, props held, condition (dirt/wet/wounds/hair). Complete in itself — never a diff against a previous state, never 'as before'. Downstream prose passes read THIS field, so keep all the detail here even where it does not earn a new signature.

from.description: The SECTION id at which this state comes into force — 'scene_12'. Must be a scene that exists in THIS chapter's own range. For a character's FIRST state, use the first scene of this chapter in which that character appears. The state holds from this scene until the next state's `from`, so this is the only positional information needed.

change.description: One short phrase naming what visibly changed at `from` (e.g. 'removes the blazer, puts on a white cotton top'). Use the empty string for a character's FIRST state in the story, which changed from nothing. If this state continues an appearance already established in a PREVIOUS chapter, also use the empty string and reuse that chapter's signature.

locations.description: LOCATIONS whose own appearance materially CHANGES within this chapter — daylight to night, a room before and after it is wrecked, a season turning, the lights cut. Each entry therefore needs at least TWO states (the before and the after). Most chapters need NONE of these: use an empty array. A location that simply recurs across scenes unchanged must NOT appear here — its anchor plate already covers it, and adding it mints a wasted identity plate.

states.description: Ordered appearance timeline for this location, same rules as a character's: one entry per material change, each holding from its `from` scene onward. MINIMUM TWO ENTRIES — a location with only one state is by definition unchanging, and its look is already covered by its anchor plate, so it does not belong in this array at all. If a location never changes on screen, OMIT it. This is a structural rule rather than a request: a single-state location entry is invalid, so the ambiguity cannot survive.

appearance.description: FULL standalone description of the location while this state holds: light, surfaces, dressing, weather, damage.

from.description: The SECTION id at which this state comes into force, e.g. 'scene_12'. Must exist in THIS chapter's range.

change.description: Short phrase naming what changed (e.g. 'day has turned to night'), or the empty string for the location's first state.
